newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower, Olivetti slumps again.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower, Olivetti slumps again.

text.p: Italian shares ended easier on Tuesday watching the retreat on Wall Street and in London while the free fall of Olivetti continued to undermine investor confidence as the shares struggled in vain to trade.

Olivetti shares kangarooed through the day's trade, tripping the automatic bourse suspension as concern over the company's financial health prompted selling. Investors await any reply Olivetti will give to 16 questions on its finances posed by bourse regulator Consob, expected after the bourse closes.
The all-share Mibtel index lost 0.68 percent to 9,588 while the Mib30 index ended off 0.8 percent at 14,337.

Olivetti shares attempted to trade throughout the day but were suspended six times and remained suspended at the close at a last quoted share price of 465.3 lire, off 9.91 percent, with a record low recorded of 465 lire.

The stock market authorities did not widened the 10 percent fluctuation limit, so the stock was suspended each time it fell the 10 percent limit. Many dealers said the shares should have been allowed to fall to find their own level.
"The continued suspensions made for an unreal situation with traders just waiting for a resumption to sell yet again," said one Milan share trader.
Carlo De Benedetti holding companies CIR and Cofide saw sharp share price declines, off 7.65 percent at 590.2 lire and 2.58 percent down at 373.6 lire respectivily.

Among other blue chips ENI gained 0.07 percent to 7,001 lire ahead of first half results later today. Fiat lost 1.8 percent to 4,267 lire after group's unit Snia reported late Monday a first half 1996 loss before tax and interest of 3.1 billion against a 5.9 billion loss in the first half 1995.
